rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test the core multimodal hypothesis. This configuration tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, which clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform unimodal baselines. It addresses the most critical design choice (modality combination) with minimal complexity, providing foundational insights before exploring more specialized configurations.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with pca_n2000 and resnet50 have moderate performance. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted improves validation accuracy, directly clarifying the impact of fusion strategies. It is the best next step as it builds on the previous experiment's setup, reducing uncertainty about a key design choice (fusion type) without repeating prior configurations.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and resnet50 image encoder achieve ~0.52 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with a larger imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other settings identical (aggregation=None, fusion=concat). This clarifies whether the image encoder's capacity significantly impacts performance, a critical design choice. It balances exploration of a key component (image encoder) with minimal changes to the existing promising setup.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_022) outperforms resnet50, and concat fusion (config_016) is better than weighted fusion. However, all prior experiments used singleprofile and no aggregation. This experiment tests the same high-performing image encoder and concat fusion with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation, clarifying whether aggregation methods and profile settings significantly impact performance. It balances exploitation of strong image encoder choices with exploration of critical design decisions (aggregation, profile setting) that remain untested.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and avgpool aggregation achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.628697). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_025) improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It is a logical extension of the top-performing configuration and addresses a critical design choice (fusion method) that could significantly affect performance.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (a more complex method) further improves performance, clarifying the impact of aggregation strategy. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation method) that could yield significant gains.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (config_025: 0.6352). This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the same high-performing configuration, clarifying whether the RNA encoder choice impacts performance. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile/avgpool/weighted pattern while exploring a promising RNA encoder variant.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (config_037: 0.706). This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) with weighted fusion further improves performance, clarifying the impact of aggregation methods on model effectiveness. It is a logical extension of the promising scvi_n200 + weighted fusion direction.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (a different design choice) in the same high-performing setup can further improve accuracy, clarifying the impact of RNA encoder selection. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly compares two key design decisions (RNA encoder) in a proven effective configuration, balancing exploitation of current success with exploration of alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could clarify whether the fusion method (concat vs weighted) impacts performance when using scgpt. It reduces uncertainty about the optimal fusion strategy for scgpt, which has shown mixed results (config_051: 0.520).
